name: St. Johann in Tirol
kurzbeschreibung: Village community in the Leukental valley between the Kaisergebirge and Kitzbüheler Alpen – pure active holiday.
beschreibung:
St. Johann in Tirol lies at 659 metres above sea level in the Leukental, directly at the intersection between the rugged Kaisergebirge to the north and the gentler Kitzbüheler Alpen to the south. The town has around 9,800 inhabitants and belongs to the district of Kufstein – as the second-largest town in the valley, it forms the economic centre of the region.

What makes St. Johann special is this direct confrontation of two completely different mountain worlds: on one side rise the striking rock faces of the Wilder Kaiser with Totenkirchl and Karlspitzen, which count among the most difficult climbing mountains in the Ostalpen. On the other side, the green slopes of the Kitzbüheler Alpen entice with easier hikes and mountain bike tours. In winter, the gondola connects the ski area on the Harschbichl with the Steinplatte, and the illuminated night ski slope is a classic for families. The Kitzbüheler Ache flows right through the town and offers popular swimming spots in summer.

Culturally, St. Johann is not a high-gloss destination like neighbouring Kitzbühel, but down-to-earth. The parish church with its baroque tower shapes the townscape, and in summer the village evenings with brass bands provide genuine Tiroler flair. Culinarily, the traditional inns around the Hauptplatz are worthwhile – Kaiserschmarrn and Kaspressknödel are still served here where they have been cooked for generations.
